ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system of the $x O y$ plane, there is a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction intensity $B$ perpendicular to the $x O y$ plane and pointing inward within the right triangle $MNL$. One of the right-angle sides $ML$ has a length of $6a$ and lies on the $y$-axis, with $\angle NML = 30^{\circ}$, and its midline $OP$ lies on the $x$-axis. An electron beam with the same velocity $v_{0}$ is injected into the magnetic field perpendicular to the $y$-axis and the direction of the magnetic field from the interval $-3a \leq y \leq 0$ on the $y$-axis. It is known that the trajectory of the electron injected into the magnetic field from the point $y = -2a$ on the $y$-axis passes exactly through the point $O$. If a uniform electric field with magnitude $E = Bv_{0}$ and direction along the positive $y$-axis is added in the first quadrant region of the Cartesian coordinate system $x O y$, and a planar fluorescent screen is placed perpendicular to the $x$-axis at $x = 3a$, intersecting the $x$-axis at point $Q$, ignoring the interactions between electrons and neglecting the gravity of the electrons, determine:

1. What is the specific charge of an electron?
2. What is the range of the y-coordinate for the electron beam entering the electric field from the $+y$ axis?
3. What is the maximum distance from point $Q$ on the fluorescent screen that an electron, entering the electric field perpendicular to the $y$-axis from the magnetic field, can reach?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, O is taken as the coordinate origin, the y-axis is vertical, and the x-axis is horizontal. Triangle MNL is located on the left side of the y-axis, ML is on the y-axis, M is above O, L is below O, and the length ML=6a, so M=(0,3a) and L=(0,-3a) may be set. The hypotenuse MN slopes toward the lower left, ∠NML=30° is marked in the figure, and P is the intersection point of the hypotenuse and the x-axis. Crosses are drawn inside the triangular region, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper inward. Electrons enter the magnetic field from positions on the y-axis with -3a≤y≤0 at speed v0 to the left. Upward electric field arrows E are drawn in the first quadrant, and there is a vertical fluorescent screen on the right, intersecting the x-axis at Q; the problem states that the screen is at x=3a. Reasoning: When the electron is negatively charged, the velocity is to the left, and the magnetic field is inward, the Lorentz force makes its trajectory curve upward. Suppose an electron enters the magnetic field at y=y0 and the trajectory radius is R, then the center of the circle is on the y-axis, with coordinates (0,y0+R). It is known that the electron trajectory entering from y0=-2a just passes through O. The distance from this circle center to the incident point (0,-2a) is R, and the distance to O is also R, therefore |(-2a+R)-0|=R, giving R=a. From R=mv0/(eB), the electron specific charge is e/m=v0/(Ba). For a general incident point y0∈[-3a,0], the circular trajectory intersects the y-axis again at y=y0+2R=y0+2a, and at this time the velocity direction is to the right, entering the first-quadrant electric field. Requiring the entry point to be on the +y-axis means y≥0, so y0≥-2a. Also y0≤0, therefore the height range entering the electric field is y=y0+2a, hence 0≤y≤2a. After entering the first-quadrant electric field, the electron moves rightward from (0,y) with vx=v0 and vy=0. The electric field direction is upward, and the electron is subjected to an electric-field force downward, with acceleration magnitude A=(e/m)E=(v0/(Ba))·Bv0=v0^2/a. Therefore, in the first quadrant the trajectory satisfies y(x)=y-x^2/(2a). When the electron reaches the x-axis, 0=y-x1^2/(2a), so x1=sqrt(2ay). Since 0≤y≤2a, x1≤2a<3a, and the electron has already left the first-quadrant electric field before reaching the screen. When reaching the x-axis, the vertical velocity vy=-A(x1/v0)=-v0 sqrt(2y/a); afterward it moves at uniform speed in a straight line in the field-free region to x=3a. The downward distance on the screen relative to Q is d(y)=sqrt(2y/a)·(3a-sqrt(2ay)). Let s=sqrt(2y/a), then s∈[0,2], and d=a(3s-s^2). This quadratic function takes its maximum at s=3/2, dmax=a(9/2-9/4)=9a/4.
